text: Doom. A prediction market where the odds are public, and the bettors are not.
Prediction markets work because you can see the money. That is also the problem.
Wallets are public. Anyone can follow the biggest positions, and the crowd follows the bettor instead of the evidence.
Doom splits them apart. Bet sizes, odds and volume stay public, and that keeps the market accurate. Who is betting never touches the chain.
It is a real market maker over binary outcome shares.
Volume is public. Bettor identities on chain: zero.
Thirteen markets, live on Starknet mainnet.
Every price is a probability, read off the contract.
Here is a bet. First, shield your tokens into Starknet's privacy pool.
Pick a market. Bitcoin above one hundred fifty thousand. The market says fifty five percent.
Choose a side, and a stake.
The panel calls the contract's own quote, so what you see is what you get.
The pool calls the market. The pool is always the caller, so the contract never sees an address.
Four transactions on mainnet. Four different senders. None of them is the bettor's wallet.
The odds move. The market learned something. It never learned who.
One honest limitation. Claiming links a payout back to the bet, though never to a person.
Collateral is measured by balance change, not calldata. Positions key off a commitment, not an address.
Settlement is bonded. Anyone proposes, anyone disputes by matching the bond, and an arbiter only touches a contested market.
Fourteen contracts. Thirteen markets. Fifty five passing tests. Zero bettor identities.
Doom. Visible odds. Invisible bettors.
